Annotate

/AN-uh-tayt/ - the stress falls on AN · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Annotate means to add explanatory notes to a text.

The star pitcher annotates every scouting report, jotting beside each batter's name the pitch that got him out last season.

Worked Example

When the software team inherited a decade-old codebase, the departing engineer spent her final week annotating it: short notes above the strangest functions, saying why each odd fix exists and what breaks without it.

Annotate is more specific than 'write on' or 'mark up' because the additions must explain something — an annotation carries information about the text it sits beside, not just a stray underline or doodle.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

gloss: to add a brief definition of a single hard word — an annotation can do far more

footnote: to add references at the page's bottom; annotations usually sit right beside the text

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

skim: to slide over a text quickly, leaving no trace of your thinking

erase: to remove marks rather than add them

Where it sits · how much the marking actually tells you — underline → highlight → annotate

underline vs. annotate: Underline stops far short of annotate — a line under a phrase says 'this matters' without saying why.

highlight vs. annotate: Highlight goes further than underline — color instead of a thin line — but it still adds no words; annotate tops the ladder by leaving actual explanations on the page.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — an-

Prefix — an-: to, toward (Latin ad-, reshaped before n)

Root — not

Root — not: a mark, a note (Latin nota)

Suffix — -ate

Suffix — -ate: to make, to do

Put it together

Put it together: Latin ad- ('to') slides into an- before an n, and nota is a mark: annotare meant 'to put marks to' a text. Add the verb-making -ate and you have annotate — literally to attach notes.

Use the root in a new word: denote

Use the root in a new word: denote: On the weather map, a red triangle denotes a station reporting severe wind.

Word Choice

neutral / academic

Annotate is the working scholar's verb: notes are added to a text to explain it. If the note merely defines one word, gloss is narrower; if you are explaining at length in your own essay rather than in the margins, you are closer to explicate, this unit's word for full-dress explanation.
